neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that on 25.03.1999, two individuals on a scooter fired at the victim-deceased and snatched a money bag from him. When PW-2 tried to stop them, he was also shot. The assailants fled away. The victim-deceased was found dead at the scene, and PW-2 was injured. The police could not identify the culprits for several years until information led to the arrest of the two accused-appellants. The trial court convicted them under sections 302, 307, and 397 IPC read with Section 34 IPC. The High Court upheld the conviction. The accused were identified by eyewitnesses PW-2 and PW-3, who described the incident in detail. PW-2, the injured witness, testified that the accused shot the victim-deceased and then fired at him before fleeing. The incident lasted for 90 seconds, and PW-2 became unconscious after being shot. The medical evidence confirmed the injuries were caused by a firearm. The accused refused to participate in the identification parade, but the courts accepted the eyewitness accounts and the medical evidence as credible.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the appellants were the perpetrators of the crime, as evidenced by the eyewitness accounts of PW-2 and PW-3, and that the appellants had confessed to the crime before PW-1, who was a respected community leader.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the appellants could not be identified after 7 years due to the passage of time and the lack of previous acquaintance with the witnesses, and that the testimony of PW-2 was unreliable due to the lapse of time and the possibility of memory fading.

quotes.text: The argument raised that it was difficult to remember the faces of the accused persons after 7 years of incident particularly in the absence of previous acquaintance not tenable as the assailants shot dead the companion of PW-2 and also fired at PW-2 and for PW-2 it was horror scene resulting in traumatic experience.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that memory is not a video recorder and that the circumstances under which an event is witnessed significantly affect the reliability of the memory, especially in cases involving trauma and severe injury.

quotes.text: Memory does not work like a video recorder. Instead, when a person witnesses some complex event, such as a crime, he or she acquires fragments of information from the environment.
